newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters defends coalition-building compromise.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters defends coalition-building compromise.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters on Friday defended compromises his New Zealand First Party had made to form a coalition government and rejected accusations it had "sold out".

"We freely admit that compromises were made with National. But let us not forget that significant compromises were also made by National and, at the end of the day, our gains outweighed ouur losses," Peters said in a speech to a Maritime Museum fundraising lunch.
"Broken promises under a first-past-the-post system are not comparable to essential compromises made under MMP," he said.

Nationalist New Zealand First formed a coalition with the conservative National Party in December after negotiating separately with National and centre-left Labour in the wake of October's general election.
The election was the first to be held under the German-style mixed-member proportional electoral system.
Peters said it was only on election night his party realised the enormity of its position.
"And for all Labour's attacks that New Zealand First 'sold out' to National it was our refusal to do just that that ultimately jeopardised a successful coalition with Labour."
He said Labour expected unacceptable compromises from NZ First with few gains in return.
